items.stem: What does visual hierarchy do in a design?

options.text: Guides the viewer's eye to the most important elements first
options.rationale: Correct: hierarchy controls reading order and emphasis.

options.text: Makes every element the same size for fairness
Adds as many colours as possible
options.rationale: More colour does not create hierarchy.

options.text: Removes all text from the layout
options.rationale: Hierarchy organises content, it does not remove it.

items.explanation: Correct: hierarchy controls reading order and emphasis.

items.stem: A flyer must be printed professionally and also posted on social media. Which TWO file choices are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A high-resolution CMYK file for professional print
options.rationale: Correct: print needs CMYK at high resolution (e.g. 300 dpi).

options.text: An RGB export sized for the social platform
options.rationale: Correct: screens use RGB at the platform's pixel dimensions.

options.text: A single low-resolution RGB file for both uses
options.rationale: Low-resolution RGB prints poorly and ignores colour mode.

options.text: A print file in RGB at 72 dpi
options.rationale: 72 dpi RGB is for screen, not professional print.

items.explanation: Correct: CMYK high-res for print and RGB sized for screen.

items.stem: A layout feels cluttered and hard to scan. Which principle most directly helps?

options.text: Alignment and proximity to group and organise elements
options.rationale: Correct: aligning and grouping related items creates order and scannability.
White space aids clarity; removing it harms it.

items.explanation: Correct: aligning and grouping related items creates order and scannability.
